questions.prompt: Why should the input be sorted before constructing subsets?

choices.label: To remove all repeated values from the input.
choices.feedback: Sorting groups equal alternatives without discarding repeated positions that may belong in a valid subset.

choices.label: To ensure only subsets of consecutive values are produced.
choices.feedback: Sorting groups equal alternatives without discarding repeated positions that may belong in a valid subset.

choices.label: To place equal values together for duplicate-choice checks.
choices.feedback: Sorting groups equal alternatives without discarding repeated positions that may belong in a valid subset.

questions.prompt: Which equal values should be skipped at a given recursion depth?

choices.label: Later equal alternatives to the first choice at that depth.
choices.feedback: Sibling choices with the same value create duplicate subsets. Equal values can still be selected together at different depths.

choices.label: None; every identical branch should produce another answer.
choices.feedback: Sibling choices with the same value create duplicate subsets. Equal values can still be selected together at different depths.

choices.label: Every equal value anywhere deeper in the recursion.
choices.feedback: Sibling choices with the same value create duplicate subsets. Equal values can still be selected together at different depths.

questions.prompt: When should the current subset be recorded?

choices.label: Only when it uses every input position.
choices.feedback: Subsets of every size are valid, and a subset may contain multiple copies when the input has them.

choices.label: Only when it contains no repeated values.
choices.feedback: Subsets of every size are valid, and a subset may contain multiple copies when the input has them.

choices.label: At every call, including the empty subset.
choices.feedback: Subsets of every size are valid, and a subset may contain multiple copies when the input has them.
